help.title: Help
help.lead: App guide - shortcuts, editing, parameters and where everything lives.
help.body.keys:
Ctrl+Alt+E - inspector (select and edit the HUD)
Ctrl+Alt+H - show / hide the HUD
Ctrl+Alt+I - identify monitors (OSD cards with layout)
Ctrl+Alt+C - copy the layout under the cursor to clipboard
Ctrl+Alt+R - reload layout from disk (after editing the file)
Ctrl+Alt+F1 - this help
Ctrl+Alt+A - copy hex color of the pixel under the cursor (magnifier)
Ctrl+Alt+X - quit the app
Ctrl+Alt+Q - magnifier on/off
Default shortcuts can be remapped on the Shortcuts card.
help.body.edit:
Ctrl+Alt+E opens edit mode: right-click the canvas for new elements (value, bar, graph, box, text, image, grid). Drag = move, handles = resize, Ctrl+click or rubber band = group select, arrows = nudge, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y = undo / redo, Del = delete.
Double-click an element to open the inspector: colors, font, size, background; for values a prop binding (SimHub telemetry, Sys.*, Eq.*) and units. Saving is automatic - the same layout on other monitors syncs by itself.
A layout is a JSON file - edit it in notepad too, then Ctrl+Alt+R picks up the changes.
The magnifier checkbox in the inspector enables a zoomed view under the cursor; general editor settings also live in Control Center → Inspector.
help.body.grids:
Grid = a cell mesh as one element: flat = flat table, persp = 3D platform with a vanishing point. An element dropped into a grid becomes a member - grid drags and resizes carry it (dragging it out releases it). fill = eq fills cells with the spectrum.
The vanishing point drags like a handle: Ctrl+Shift = platform grows with the frame, Alt+Shift = clip inside the frame; the floating ◀ ◎ ▶ tilts / centers the angle. Dragging the point through the whole platform flips it to the ceiling.
help.body.widgets:
A widget is a native bar of live values - no WebView, it runs without the HUD and in lite mode. Management: its own Widgets item in the Control Center navigation; tray → Widgets toggles individual ones, "manage" opens the standalone window.
Position: docked to a monitor edge or "free". Horizontal/vertical orientation is chosen independently of docking.
Edit mode (Ctrl+Alt+E): the left button drags ANY widget - pull a docked one into the middle and it stays free, dropping it near an edge re-docks it (glowing marks at the edges show the active one). Left click = widget inspector, right click = menu: on, docking, inspector, remove. Outside edit the widget is click-through.
Look: theme from a dropdown (look presets), widget alpha, background alpha, corner radius (empty = capsule), custom name shown in tray.
Add items on the Widgets page - each has a prop, label, unit and color. The content also feeds RTSS OSD - text right inside the game, even in exclusive fullscreen.
help.body.feat:
HUD layouts on each monitor separately (tray → Layouts).
SimHub telemetry ~60 Hz via our plugin - racing data, delta, flags.
EQ spectrum from PC audio, hardware sensor monitoring, media info.
Fans and curves, system cleanup, startup & task management, ping.
Software - installed programs inventory and batch uninstall: check what you want, uninstallers pop up one by one on their own (silent when the vendor provides it, or forced per toolkit), summary + uninstall log.
Widgets - native value bars with free positioning, edit-mode dragging, themes and RTSS in-game output.
Render engine per monitor: webview (full graphics), native (no WebView process, less RAM) or wallpaper - the inspector look gets baked right into the desktop wallpaper.
HW info: basic overview or maxi inventory - which one the menu item opens is chosen by a checkbox in Settings → System.
Hardware detection on par with the most-used tools (CPU-Z/GPU-Z/HWiNFO) - and crucially: every value is a bindable prop. The app offers 1,565 props, all routable to HUDs, widgets, RTSS overlays, alerts and fan logic - competitors only show them in their own window.
Smart resource supervision - a checkbox grants permission, a source runs only while something consumes it (EQ/LHM/DX stop on their own when nothing needs them). Live source states with reasons + own usage on the Sources page.
Data sources: auto / demo / SimHub; themes, scaling and languages in the Control Center.
help.body.args:
chicago.exe /settings = Control Center · /fans · /widgets · /cleaner · /startup · /tasks · /swinfo · /hwinfo · /hwmaxi · /dxtest · /about · /donate · /help
/clean and /clean-bin = silent cleanup · /lite · /full · /tools
/debug = debug mode · /applog = app log · /source:auto|demo|simhub · /lang:code · /scale:percent or 0 · /layout:file
· /edit[:on|off] = inspector mode · /inspektor = inspector window · /zoom[:on|off] = magnifier · /color = hex color to clipboard · /quit = exit
help.body.paths:
data\layouts = your layouts (JSON) · data\settings.json · data\log.txt · data\lang = custom translations · data\exports = tool outputs (csv, uninstall log).
Sample layouts live in the layout folder next to chicago.exe. Open the data folder from the Control Center, Files page.

h.zoom: zoomed view under the cursor - pixel-precise element placement
f.label: label
f.showHint: expr: v < 60 · v == 1 · d.Flag_Blue - empty = always
h.gmode: flat = even cells for grouping · persp = vanishing floor to horizon (synthwave)
h.gcols: number of columns (persp: vertical rays from vanish point)
h.grows: number of rows (persp: horizontal lines to horizon)
h.ghor: horizon position as fraction of element height (0 = top, 1 = bottom)
h.gvan: x of vanish point as fraction of width (0.5 = center)
h.gcomp: row compression to top edge - higher = denser on top (real perspective 2-3)
h.ganim: speed of rows rolling toward the viewer (0 = off, ~30 = lively floor)
h.gstop: how far rays reach toward the vanish point - 0 = all the way, 0.3 = trapezoid 3D platform/stage
h.gspread: platform bottom width as multiple of element width - 1 = whole platform inside, >1 = overhang
h.gdepth: smallest inherited font scale at platform top edge - 0 = down to a point, 0.3 = keeps 30%
h.gfill: eq = cells fill by channel level in each column (spectrum on the platform)
h.gprop: channel prop base name - column i reads 'propBase+i' (or {i} in text), default Eq.Band
h.gflip: mirrored platform - hangs from top as ceiling, vanish point below; auto-flip by dragging handle past middle
h.gfont: parent font - inherited by elements with 'inherit from grid' inside the grid
h.gfontSize: parent font size for inheriting elements
h.gweight: parent font weight for inheriting elements
h.tcolor: parent text color for inheriting elements
h.usz: unit size in em for inheriting elements
h.inherit: font/color/unit inherited from the grid under the element - own values fill the gaps
prof.h: process (.exe optional) or SimHub game name (partial match) → monitor → layout; "HUD off" hides that monitor; everything reverts when the game exits
al.h: fires when the threshold is crossed (then again only after it drops back); key = telemetry id (Sys.CpuTemp, Gpu.Temp…), voice = Windows speech voice, "quiet" = pause in seconds between repeats
al.cd.h: minimum pause in seconds between repeats while the condition holds
fan.on.h: turning off restores fans to hardware-auto and blocks all writes - the tray menu has the same toggle
fan.h: manual keeps a 20% floor; curve = % by temperature between two anchor points (flat outside, 4% hysteresis); everything returns to hardware-auto on critical temperature, HW source off, clean exit or app crash (watched by a guardian process)
fan.guard.h: watchdog process - when the app dies or freezes it restores fans to hardware-auto; it starts only while manual/curve writes are active, otherwise idle
fan.more: motherboard fans lack a control channel - they need the PawnIO driver (bundled with the installer) and admin rights; hit "rescan" after installing
fan.none: no controllable channels - enable the HW sensors aux source (GPU/HW) on the Sources tab
fan.noPawn: PawnIO driver not found - motherboard fans and temperatures cannot be detected; it is bundled with the installer (or pawnio.eu)
fan.noAdmin: without admin rights detection may be incomplete - depending on the board some fans and sensors may not show
fan.admin.h: motherboard fans and temperatures need admin rights - the app will restart (one UAC prompt)
fan.conflict: is running - it may overwrite values and hold controller access
fan.tug: is writing to fans you also control here - two apps fight over control and RPM may oscillate
fo.title: fan control options
fo.head: fan control options
fo.off: fan control is off - enable it in control options or the tray menu
fo.usbxp.h: SiUSBXp = Silicon Labs Direct Access driver for Asetek 690LC coolers (EVGA CLC, NZXT Kraken X, Corsair Hydro GTX/v2); the installer can bundle it, or download it from the official page
fo.gduty.h: where a channel returns on "auto"/guardian restore when the pre-takeover value could not be read (some usb controllers don't report duty) - applies to the app and the guardian process
set.canvas.h: x/y/w/h area (px) - x/y is the offset from the monitor's top-left corner, kept inside it; elements outside are hidden; moving the area moves the HUD as one
h.dock: monitor edge the bar sticks to
h.pitems: widget cells - prop + label + unit + color; the widget has no coordinates, you can't break it by dragging
f.visHint: e.g. <60 hides at 60+ · =1 shows only at 1 · !=0 hides 0
sys.vendorSw: vendor software running - may block usb controller readings
sys.hw.none: no hardware detected - enable gpu aux source
cyc.h: a key or wheel/button-box button triggers the chosen action - works in-game; cycle layouts runs through all layouts on the chosen monitor + off
str.h: for fan-curve tuning and tune-lab; gpu burn runs in its own window, independent of the HUD

h.textFont: font for units and non-seg7 texts
h.bgNew: background template for NEW elements (existing keep theirs)

h.maxGraph: axis high - empty = auto from history
h.orient: h horizontal · v vertical · c centered (±delta)

h.fill: solid single color · sharp hard zones · gradient smooth blend · spectrum hue-wheel sweep - all from color/color2/color3

h.seg: draw fill as LED segments with gaps
